C2_PERSISTENT_LATER_REVISION.reason: Zero relations attached to canonical_reservations support multiple committed revisions under stable reservation identity. All attached relations either enforce UNIQUE(reservation_id) (1:1) or are strictly bounded to cancellation lifecycle events and release evidence.

C3_FULL_EFFECTIVE_ALLOCATION_SNAPSHOT.reason: Zero relations store a full effective allocation snapshot for a revision N+1. canonical_reservation_nights has UNIQUE(reservation_id, stay_date) and stores only immutable V1 allocation truth under trigger protection. No revision snapshot table exists.

C4_CURRENT_EFFECTIVE_REVISION.reason: No column, pointer, or projection view exists that identifies which revision is currently effective. canonical_reservation_lifecycle_current projects lifecycle state only from V1 reservation truth.

C5_COMMERCIAL_VERSION_BINDING.reason: No relation exists that binds an N+1 reservation revision to an updated commercial quote, accepted offer revision, or price delta. Commercial truth is immutable on V1 canonical_reservations and canonical_payable_authorities.

C6_ALLOCATION_COMMERCIAL_LOCKSTEP.reason: Because no persistent later revision exists, there is zero unified version counter under which allocation and commercial versions advance together without drift.

C7_DURABLE_MODIFICATION_COMMAND_REPLAY.reason: Existing command ledgers (canonical_reservation_commands, canonical_reservation_lifecycle_commands) are strictly scoped to initial finalization and cancellation lifecycle events. Zero command ledger exists for modification requests or execution replay.

C8_CONTROLLED_REVISION_WRITER.reason: Zero accepted PL/pgSQL procedures or database routines exist that can write or commit a later reservation revision. All 5 accepted writers are bounded to hold cleanup, V1 finalization, payment composition, or cancellation.

C9_ACTIVE_MODIFICATION_SEMANTICS.reason: Zero accepted writer can replace an effective reservation allocation while preserving the reservation as the same logical ACTIVE reservation. The only accepted inventory release authority is cancellation, which moves the reservation to terminal CANCELLED.

runtimeRiskRegister.disposition: Legacy bookings table is unconstrained and non-canonical; it does not represent canonical W4-C N+1 authority.
Calendar blocking marks inventory unavailable but creates zero reservation truth; it is not an allocation replacement.
Inventory holds represent ephemeral pre-booking reservations; expiring or acquiring holds cannot publish later reservation revisions.
Cancelling and creating a new reservation loses stable identity, destroys payment binding, and introduces inventory race conditions.
